what_its_for: Minoxidil is used to help regrow hair and slow down hair loss in men and women. It works by increasing blood flow to the hair follicles, which can help hair grow back thicker and fuller. It is applied directly to the scalp where hair is thinning.
how_to_take: Apply minoxidil directly to the dry scalp in the area where your hair is thinning. If using the liquid, use the dropper or applicator to apply it directly to the scalp — do not pour it on your hair. If using the foam, part your hair and apply the foam directly to the scalp with your fingers. Gently spread it across the thinning area. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water right after applying. Do not use a hair dryer on the treated area immediately after applying. Let it dry naturally for at least 2 to 4 hours before going to bed or getting the scalp wet.
dosing: Adults: Apply 1 mL of the 2% or 5% liquid solution, OR half a capful of foam, to the affected scalp area twice daily (morning and evening). Do not use more than directed — using extra will not speed up hair growth and may increase side effects. The usual daily dose is no more than 2 mL of liquid or 1 capful of foam total per day.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and just apply your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not apply a double dose to make up for the missed one. Consistency is important — try to apply it at the same times each day for best results.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat and open flames — the foam and liquid forms can be flammable. Keep the container tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze. Do not store in the bathroom where humidity and heat can damage the product.
what_to_avoid: Do not apply to skin that is red, irritated, infected, or sunburned. Do not use on any part of the body other than the scalp. Avoid getting minoxidil in your eyes, mouth, or nose. If contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. Do not use other scalp products (like styling gels or hairsprays) immediately after applying minoxidil — let it dry first. Avoid letting children or pets come into contact with treated areas. Do not use if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: chest pain, a fast or irregular heartbeat, sudden unexplained weight gain, swelling in your hands, feet, or face, dizziness or lightheadedness, severe scalp irritation, redness, rash, or itching that does not go away, or unwanted facial hair growth. Also call your doctor if you do not see any improvement after using the product for 4 to 6 months, or if your hair loss gets worse.
when_it_works: Minoxidil takes time to work. Most people begin to see results after using it consistently for 3 to 6 months. Some people may notice increased hair shedding in the first few weeks — this is normal and usually means the product is working. Do not stop using it without talking to your doctor, because hair loss will return within a few months of stopping treatment.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects of minoxidil. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Do not use without first consulting your doctor. Children under 18: Not recommended unless directed by a doctor. People with heart disease or high blood pressure: Talk to your doctor before using, as minoxidil can affect blood pressure and heart rate. People with kidney or liver problems: Consult your doctor before use.
